Asha (new-hire): hey folks — quick network help. First week getting set up. I'm SSHing to bastion.us-east-1.redwood from my M1 MacBook and the session randomly drops after ~5-10 minutes. Also noticed git fetch over the jump intermittently fails with "DNS lookup failed". Anyone seen this with split-tunnel WireGuard + our bastion?

Tom R. (infra): welcome! common cause is client-side keepalive + split-tunnel DNS. two quick things to try: set ServerAliveInterval on client and ensure your WireGuard is routing internal DNS to 10.0.0.2. can you paste your ~/.ssh/config for the host?

Asha (new-hire): thanks. here's the host entry I'm using:

```
Host bastion.redwood
  HostName bastion.us-east-1.redwood
  User asha
  ForwardAgent yes
  ProxyCommand ssh -W %h:%p jump.redwood
```

Tom R. (infra): a few suggestions: add ServerAliveInterval 30 and ServerAliveCountMax 3 to that host stanza. also try ProxyJump instead of ProxyCommand: `ProxyJump jump.redwood`. finally, on macOS the ssh-agent sometimes stops when the keychain or gpg-agent interacts — run `ssh -vvv` while reproducing and paste the lines around the disconnect. :eyes:

Priya S. (it-support): @Asha also double-check your WireGuard client has `AllowedIPs` set to include 10.0.0.0/8 for internal services or at least the internal DNS subnet. Split-tunnel setups often leave DNS queries going to the public resolver which causes intermittent NXDOMAIN/errors. If you can't change the client, add a local /etc/hosts or resolv override for gitlab.redwood until we fix routing.

Asha (new-hire): here's the ssh -vvv snippet when it died:

```
debug1: client_input_global_request: rtype hostkeys-00@openssh.com want_reply 0
debug1: channel 0: rcvd ext data 1
debug1: channel 0: rcvd ext data 2
debug1: channel 0: rcvd eof
Read from socket failed: Connection reset by peer
```

Tom R. (infra): "Connection reset by peer" usually means the TCP connection got killed, not SSH itself. That matches the WG split-tunnel DNS/route flip or a sleepy NAT/firewall on your ISP. Try adding to ~/.ssh/config:

```
Host bastion.redwood
  ServerAliveInterval 30
  ServerAliveCountMax 3
  TCPKeepAlive yes
  ProxyJump jump.redwood
```

Also, under System Preferences > Network > Advanced > TCP/IP, ensure the primary interface isn't toggling. For a quick repro, run `ping -i 10 10.0.0.1` to keep the route active.

deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance: bastion-2 will be restarted in 10m for kernel updates — this may affect current sessions. (ID: maint-2026-03-23-1) :warning:

Ops Oncall: confirming — we just kicked a rolling reboot on bastion-2. If you were on that host, sessions could drop. Use `ssh bastion.redwood -J jump.redwood` to jump to other bastions while we finish.

Asha (new-hire): ah ok that explains intermittent drops — I caught it while you were rebooting. I added ServerAliveInterval and switched to ProxyJump; so far stable. Still saw one DNS hiccup, Priya's suggestion to point `nameserver 10.0.0.2` in my WireGuard DNS config fixed it. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:

Tom R. (infra): welcome aboard! If the agent forwarding stops working after a reboot, run `ssh-add -l` on your machine and `ssh -A` from the jump. If you want, ping me and I can pair for a quick troubleshooting session.

Priya S. (it-support): added a small onboarding note to the new-hire checklist: "If using split-tunnel VPN, ensure internal DNS is routed and set ServerAliveInterval for bastion sessions." I'll follow up with an M1-specific note about keychain/ssh-agent quirks.

Asha (new-hire): perfect — appreciate the fast help!
